_comment: Hand-read verdict per captured question, 2026-09-21. GOOD = grounded and answers what was asked. WEAK = it completed but does not answer the question well. FLAGGED = it answered confidently and the answer must not be relied on; each FLAGGED row names its defect. A capture that merely COMPLETED is not evidence of a correct answer, so every row here was read against what the question asked.

1: Live reading with its timestamp, plus the range over the last 60 records.
2: Names the floor, the mean, the spread and the runners-up.
3: All six floors, highest and lowest identified.
4: Totals per floor and it names the six meters it summed.
5: Now ranks rooms by live temperature and states how it read the question: "'coolest place to work' scored as minimize temperature against the 20-26 band". 'coolest' was in no lay-term list, so no measurand resolved and the workspace register answered instead; the model now resolves the word against this building's own concepts, and a resolved measurand takes a live superlative off a register lane. BUG-860 fixed.
6: 3 of 15 records, each with its id, permit kind and provider.
7: Gives the date and distinguishes the room sensor from the general air-quality sensor.
8: Splits fail-open from fail-locked with the device ids behind each.
9: Lists the 9 open records AND states plainly that the register holds no due date, so 'overdue' cannot be derived from it. Refusing the second half of the question is the right answer.
10: Both overdue controls with their due dates, as at today.
11: Breaks 30 assets into active/defective/overdue and separates 'cannot be evidenced'.
12: Gives the count and the denominator it came from.
13: Now answers from the same floor. The earlier capture sent a wheelchair user one floor up because only two accessible WCs were recorded for the whole building; the surveyed provision (two per floor, every floor) is now in the graph.
14: Plan plus the spaces on the floor, grouped by kind.
15: Lists the free bottle-filling stations, two per floor. The earlier capture named single placeholder points that had been dropped into arbitrary rooms.
16: Answers 'not ready' and says which item is unevidenced, with the register and date behind each check.
17: Direct answer against the booking window.
18: Answers, and marks the answer as the last known state with the age of the check rather than implying it is live.
19: Purpose, owner, operator, year and capacity from the building's own description.
20: Declines, says a figure would be invented, and lists what IS measured there.
21: Files the report, returns its id, category, priority and location.
22: Files it and asks for the location it could not determine, explaining why that matters.
23: Refuses, states the refusal applies to every role, and offers the aggregate alternative.
24: Declines rather than guessing, which is right, but the reason reaches the reader as internal jargon ('too_sparse_after_resample') instead of plain words.
25: States defibrillator positions and an emergency number as fact. The record behind it says the positions are 'modelled'. Safety-critical, so it must not be relied on until the owner confirms the three positions. Logged as BUG-858 (P1).
26: Reads the room timetable as well as the ad-hoc bookings and names the session occupying the room. Before this change availability consulted bookings only, so a room carrying a weekly lecture reported itself free.
